Sasha — thanks for the clear note and the model. High level answers up front, then a couple of options below that map to the scenarios you described.

Short answers:
- Yes — we support an "acceleration window" construct. We can predefine a set of months where you can accelerate up to a higher tranche without a full contract amendment; the cost delta is captured via a pre-authorized credit ladder.
- Term discounts: we typically present two structures for phased commits: (A) blended annualized rate (smoother cashflow, smaller initial discount) and (B) front-loaded prepay (larger year-1 credit that steps down). Both are available; the better economics depend on your willingness to prepay and desired flexibility.

Proposed sketch (please see attached term sheet PDF for numbers):
Option A — Blended annualized rate
- Commit: 3-year term, target capacity 100% = 16 GPUs / X TPM baseline
- Year 1 committed: 50% of target; Year 2: 75%; Year 3: 100%
- Discount: applied to annual invoice as a blended effective discount across the term (we amortize prepay credit across months). Acceleration window: up to 25% additional capacity in months M3-M6 at a pre-negotiated uplift.

Option B — Front-loaded prepay ladder (better unit economics)
- Commit: 3-year term, same capacity profile.
- Prepay structure: Year 1 prepay covers 60% of year-1 expected usage (credits on invoice), Year 2 covers 80%, Year 3 covers 100%.
- Term discount: higher for year-1 prepay (since you pay earlier) and declines thereafter. Acceleration window: covered by a draw-down of a pre-funded acceleration reserve; execution triggers a billing adjustment but no legal amendment.

I included a quick TCO table (hosted vs. dedicated) in the term sheet showing ~36% unit-cost improvement at steady-state for dedicated with the front-loaded structure vs hosted, assuming your utilization profile.

Next steps:
1) If you'd like the most aggressive unit economics, we can draft Option B numbers (including acceleration reserve sizing).
2) If procurement prefers predictable blended invoices, we'll produce Option A with blended rates.

Looping in Dylan Brooks (pricing) and Marissa Cole (account lead) to help size the acceleration reserve and finalize numbers. Happy to jump on a 30-min call Wed.

Sasha / team — thanks for the patience. After reviewing the model and internal guardrails, here is a concrete proposal that balances flexibility and unit economics.

Executive summary:
- Term: 3 years (annual invoicing, prepay credits applied monthly)
- Year-1 prepay: covers 60% of expected Y1 usage (prepaid credits applied to invoices)
- Acceleration reserve: pre-funded at 15% of total Y1 committed spend — allows bursts up to an additional 30% of capacity across months 3–6 with no contract amendment. If drawn, the reserve is consumed and future invoices reflect the draw-down.
- Year-by-year effective discounts (example): Y1: 18% off list (front-loaded), Y2: 12%, Y3: 8% (blended effective ~12.6%)
- If Altair triggers a full permanent acceleration (sustained >4 consecutive months above 100% of committed capacity), we will convert to the next tranche with a one-time reconciliation and a one-month notice; pricing will follow the pre-agreed tranche rate.

Why this approach: it keeps procurement flexibility (pre-funded reserve instead of legal amendments), provides you a predictable credit balance to draw from, and preserves strong unit economics for Altair when they commit earlier. Compared to hosted, this reduces per-token cost by ~32% at your target utilization.

2) If this aligns, procurement can sign the term sheet and we'll issue a DocuSign for the definitive SOW.
